Prevention: Clean tools and farm machinery to prevent bulbs and stolons from being spread
Use certified clean seed to avoid weed seed introduction through contamination
Do not accept potentially contaminated materials, e.g. manure and mulch
During field preparation, avoid ploughing through
Oxalis infested areas to avoid spread of weed bulbs and stolons
Monitoring: Look for small plants without short stem but with 14-15 leaves.
Each leaf is composed of 3 fishtail shaped leaflets link to each other
The bulb in the soil looks like a small whitish carrot (diameter: 1-2 cm)
Inspect fields as and when you are in the field, in particular during and shortly after the wet season, and consider direct control when found
Direct Control: Plough during dry season to expose the bulbs and stolons in the soil to be destroyed by dessication
Place organic mulch over areas where weed is expect to grow to provide temporary weed suppression
Plough and cover an infested area with a polyethylene sheet to destroy bulbs and stolons in the dry season (soil solarization) especially in the nurseries
